title: Relays: the count when a finished piece goes on
claim: Under (S3) and (S4) only: infinite pieces of the extended complex follow CHAIN-IDENT's cluster count; a finite piece (a tree of blocks without chains, occurring only when K is a tree) follows its clusters to its top at round |Y| - 1 and then, if another piece holds a live knot, carries a relay (the pendant rule applied to the top: one point with two endless chains), making k junctions in the k-th round after its top; if it is the only piece it closes (Theorem 4). For K a tree, the dimension is max(chains of an infinite piece, 2 if a piece is finite) (Theorem 5); in bare trees, two is typical because a class without chains relays (Corollary 6).
